page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c2d server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of dedicated system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25 percent of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance is weaker, falling into the bottom 25 percent for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, with read speeds of 46.82 GB/sec and write speeds of 27.55 GB/sec, while small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as PassMark CPU encryption and single-threaded gzip compression, perform at average levels. Conversely, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput show lower relative performance, placing in the bottom 25 percent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-4 offers a high-density memory configuration on dedicated AMD EPYC hardware without the added expense of local storage or GPU accelerators. This makes it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel compute scaling or local disk I/O. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive applications, single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight caching layers, and small-scale text processing or basic language model inference. It is less suited for highly parallelized compilation, multi-threaded ray tracing, or high-throughput database operations.
